title: Subscription Invoice Fetcher
summary: Upload your subscription/invoice breakdown sheet and it searches your Gmail inbox for a matching invoice email for each row, using the vendor/partner name (not the internal department name) to search, and gives you back a report showing which invoices were found, with a live row-by-row progress indicator while it runs.
prompt: Zero invoices are being matched even though the real invoice emails are sitting right there in the inbox. Root cause: the sheet has TWO different columns that both currently get treated as one — Enterprise (an internal department/cost-center label, e.g. Engineering, Admin) and Partner (Vendor) (the actual company that sent the invoice, e.g. Microsoft, Obsidian.md, Zoom). The tool is currently searching Gmail for the Enterprise value (Engineering) as the sender/company name, but Engineering is an internal department name that will never appear in any real invoice email — the vendor name (Microsoft, Zoom, etc) is what actually appears in the email sender/subject/body, and that value lives in a separate Partner (Vendor) column the tool ignores. Fix: detect a distinct vendor/partner column (keywords like vendor, partner, supplier — separate from the existing enterprise/client/company keyword group) and use THAT column'\''s value to match against the email sender/subject/body, not the enterprise/department column. Keep the enterprise/department column for display in the output report as before, just stop using it as the email-matching key. If no separate vendor/partner column exists in a given sheet, fall back to using the enterprise column for matching same as today, so sheets without this distinction still work. Separately: the tool shows a plain '\''Loading'\'' message with no progress while it works through all the rows, which can take a while against a large inbox — add a simple progress indicator (e.g. '\''Processing row 3 of 24...'\'') so it does not look stuck.
assumptions: A 'vendor/partner column' is any column whose header contains vendor, partner, or supplier - kept distinct from the enterprise/client/company/customer/organisation keyword group
Matching is a plain text search of the vendor value (or enterprise value, as fallback) against the email sender, subject, and body - not fuzzy/alias matching
The progress indicator is a simple text line updated per row via polling, not a graphical progress bar
All other matching, date, and amount logic is unchanged from the previous version
gaps: No fuzzy/alias matching - a sheet vendor name that doesn't match the wording used in the actual invoice email (e.g. sheet says AWS but the email is from Amazon Web Services) will still show as not found
Nothing is written back to the uploaded sheet - the enterprise/vendor distinction is used internally only
expects: The invoice breakdown sheet as a .xlsx file, with a header row somewhere in the first 10 rows containing columns for enterprise/department, (ideally) a separate vendor/partner/supplier column, a breakdown/description, an invoice date, and an amount
A Gmail App Password for the admin inbox to search (generated at Google Account -> Security -> 2-Step Verification -> App Passwords), entered fresh each run

history.prompt: I have attached a template subscription invoice. Across every enterprise there is a breakdown against every break down i want the invoice gotten from the admin email around that date. The feature shall take admin account access and the invoice sheet and get invoices from the gmail against every break down.

Replace the current Google OAuth sign-in flow (which needs a Cloud Console app, GMAIL_CLIENT_ID/GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET, and a redirect URI set up in advance) with a plain input field in the tool's own web page instead: an email address field and a Gmail App Password field (the 16-character password anyone can generate themselves from Google Account -> Security -> 2-Step Verification -> App Passwords, no developer setup needed). Use these two values to connect to the admin Gmail inbox over IMAP instead of the Gmail API/OAuth, and search for the invoice emails the same way as before. The app password field must be a masked password input, must never be written to disk or logged, and should only be held in memory for the current run (the user re-enters it each time they run the tool, same as they re-upload the sheet).

Sign-in is rejecting valid app passwords. The likely bug: Google displays the 16-character App Password with spaces every 4 characters for readability (e.g. 'abcd efgh ijkl mnop'), but the real password has no spaces. The current code only strips leading/trailing whitespace from the app_password field, not spaces in the middle, so a copy-pasted password with its original spacing gets sent to Gmail as-is and rejected. Fix: strip ALL whitespace from the app password (not just leading/trailing) before using it to sign in. Also update the on-page help text to mention that spaces in a pasted app password are fine and will be removed automatically.

Every row is coming back as Missing Data on a real sheet. The cause: the sheet has a title/section label in row 1 (e.g. '20001  Software Subscriptions - Engineering') and the ACTUAL column headers are in row 2 (Sr No, Voucher Number, Invoice Date, Communication / Breakdown, Partner (Vendor), Debit, Breakup Amounts, Amount in dollars, Enterprise, Test Case (reference only)). The code currently does pd.read_excel(input_path) with no header row detection, so it always treats row 1 as the header — which is wrong here, so no column ever matches and every row is marked Missing Data. Fix: instead of assuming row 1 is the header, scan the first several rows (e.g. first 10) for the row that actually looks like a header — the one containing the most recognizable column-name keywords (enterprise/client/company/vendor, breakdown/description/communication, date, amount) — and use that row as the real header, skipping any title/label rows above it. Keep everything else the same (still uses the 'Enterprise' column for enterprise name, a breakdown/description column, an invoice date column, and an amount column).
